ONCOLOGY GENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Cancer Centre

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient: [redacted name]
Age/Sex: Elderly male
MRN: [redacted ID]
Specimen Type: Bone marrow aspirate
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

CLINICAL DETAILS
Reason for Referral: Known smouldering myeloma with rising paraprotein levels
Clinical History: Patient has established diagnosis of smouldering myeloma. Recent laboratory investigations demonstrate increasing paraprotein levels, raising concern for progression to active multiple myeloma.

TEST PERFORMED
Interphase Fluorescence In Situ Hybridization (FISH)
Methodology: FISH analysis performed on CD138+ immunomagnetically purified plasma cells from bone marrow aspirate using the following probe:
- ATM (11q22.3) probe (Abbott Molecular)
- TP53 (17p13.1) probe (Abbott Molecular)

TECHNICAL DETAILS
CD138+ cell separation yield: Suboptimal
Cells analyzed: 100 interphase nuclei
Hybridization efficiency: >95%

RESULTS

ATM (11q22.3) FISH Analysis:
Result: ABNORMAL
Pattern: nuc ish (ATMx3)[68/100]
Interpretation: Three copies of ATM (11q22.3) detected in 68% of analyzed cells

TP53 (17p13.1) FISH Analysis:
Result: Unable to complete due to insufficient cell yield

ADDITIONAL FINDINGS
The CD138+ separation yielded insufficient cells for completion of the standard myeloma FISH panel. Only ATM and partial TP53 analysis could be performed.

The finding of ATM gain aligns with previous cytogenetic results showing additional numerical abnormalities in this patient.

INTERPRETATION
The presence of three copies of ATM (11q22.3) in 68% of analyzed plasma cells represents a clonal abnormality. ATM gain is a recognized cytogenetic abnormality in multiple myeloma and may be associated with disease progression. This finding, in the context of rising paraprotein levels, suggests evolution from smouldering to active multiple myeloma.

LIMITATIONS
- Incomplete FISH panel due to low CD138+ cell yield
- Unable to assess for other prognostically significant abnormalities including del(17p), t(4;14), t(14;16), and 1q gain

Reported by: [redacted name], PhD
Authorized by: [redacted name], MD, FRCPC
